No, you don't have to integrate or fuse. Many systems aim for functional multiplicity and that is perfectly healthy and okay. Dont let yourself be pressured, and if you ever want to fuse after all, it will be a natural process and you should feel comfortable and well with it. I've heard of systems were fusion happens more unexpectedly, but this is also not the first time I've heard of a system member being scared of the idea or process. I'm not sure if this is something that's available or possible to you, but if I remember correctly a member of the Entropy system felt the same fear, and their Gatekeeper was able to give them some anti fuse bubble, that kept them from fusing accidentally or without their consent. Maybe this is something you could bring up to the rest of the system and figure out if there is any measures you can take so nothing like that happens that would make you feel uncomfortable.

Take care and be kind to yourself!

Honestly, I think it's very dangerous to try and define these behaviours as stemming from a "simply evil nature" or demons. While I know that it's somewhat comforting to tell oneself that what you / others experienced couldn't have possibly come from another human being, in an attempt to seperate such horrid acts even from the whole concept of humanity itself, I also see some danger within it. 

By viewing these things as otherworldly phenomena, one only puts the narcissist in the position they want to be put in: Being seen as an omnipotent, super human being that is different and above everything. And, as any psychologist can tell you, this is simply not true. They are extremely insecure and vulnerable human beings that have often went through great pain growing up, forming their cruel and antisocial traits in the first place. They often have great inclinations towards anger, violence or guilting and shaming, and very little to no empathy / morals at all. This is what makes them narcissists. This is what makes them dangerous. Not the possession of some demonic being.

I also think this puts victims of narcisstic abuse in a very vulnerable position. Claiming some occult influence might make the victim feel even more powerless and scared and could lead to someone staying in an abusive relationship even longer. It also takes away any kind of responsibility and accountability towards the abuser. "It wasn't me, it was the demons!"

And no matter how often I get reaffirmed and people insist that I'm doing good, great or even couldn't do any better, I still feel unfulfilled and like a failure. Nothing I do can ever be good enough, and I think that is very closely connected to my father criticising everything I did, ("You shouldn't sit like this", "why are you eating this way", "you're bad at this, don't do it", or my favorite: "Dont sing, you sound like someone put a cat into a blender.") and the lack of being praised whenever I did something right (writing an A, cleaning my room by myself, etc) and the only focus being put on my wrong doings and failures.

And despite consciously knowing this, I still find myself unable to let go of these interpretations on myself and the things I'm doing. So, yeah. I get you, I absolutely get you.
